questions.question: In the elastic rebound sequence, the energy released as shaking was stored by:
options: Rock deforming elastically under strain while friction kept the fault clamped shut
Heat building up in the mantle
Water collecting in the fault
Wind loading on the mountains above

questions.question: The focus and the epicentre are, respectively:
options: Two names for the same point
The point inside the crust where the rupture starts, and the surface point vertically above it
The surface point and the point inside the crust
The strongest and weakest points of shaking

questions.question: Shallow-focus earthquakes are the world's deadliest because:
options: They occur only in cities
They last much longer
Their energy reaches the surface almost undiluted instead of being spent on the journey up
They always trigger volcanoes

questions.question: Most tremors felt around South Africa's Witwatersrand and North West goldfields — including the 2014 Orkney event — are:
options: Caused by the East African Rift
Signs of a new plate boundary
Deep-focus subduction earthquakes
Triggered by deep mining, since South Africa lies mid-plate and natural events are uncommon

subtopics.title: Seismic Waves and Locating the Epicentre

questions.question: In fixed arrival order, the three seismic wave types are:
options: P-waves, then S-waves, then surface waves
Surface waves, then S-waves, then P-waves
S-waves, then P-waves, then surface waves
All three arrive together

questions.question: Most of an earthquake's destruction is done by the surface waves because they:
options: Arrive first, catching people unaware
Are slowest but largest in amplitude, heaving and swaying the ground beneath structures
Travel through the liquid core
Move faster than sound

questions.question: The S-minus-P arrival interval at a station converts to distance because:
options: S-waves grow louder with distance
P-waves slow down over distance
The two waves leave the focus together but travel at different speeds, so their gap stretches with distance
Stations further away record fewer waves

questions.question: Three stations are the minimum for triangulation because:
options: Seismographs often break
Three readings average out errors
The law requires three observers
One distance gives a whole circle of possibilities and two circles still cross twice — only three circles intersect at a single point

subtopics.title: Richter and Mercalli — Two Different Measurements

questions.question: The Richter scale measures MAGNITUDE, which is:
options: The energy released at the focus — one value per earthquake, computed from seismogram amplitude corrected for distance
The damage observed in each town
The number of aftershocks
The depth of the focus

questions.question: Comparing magnitude 8 with magnitude 6, the correct arithmetic is:
options: Two units stronger, so about double
Ten times ten — one hundred times the ground motion — and thirty-two times thirty-two, close to one thousand times the energy
Twenty times the energy
No measurable difference

questions.question: The Mercalli scale runs I to XII and is based on:
options: Laboratory measurements of rock strength
The speed of the P-waves
Observed effects at a particular place — what people felt and what was damaged
Satellite images of the fault

questions.question: One earthquake has one Richter value but many Mercalli values because intensity:
options: Is measured in different units each time
Changes every hour after the event
Depends on the observer's mood
Varies from place to place with distance, focus depth, building quality and local ground — soft sediment amplifies shaking while bedrock passes it on lightly

questions.question: Which pairing correctly separates a PRIMARY from a SECONDARY effect?
options: Primary: buildings collapse from the shaking; secondary: fires ignited by severed gas lines
Primary: disease outbreaks; secondary: ground rupture
Primary: homelessness; secondary: collapsing bridges
Primary: economic loss; secondary: ground rupture

questions.question: Liquefaction, which undermined whole suburbs of Christchurch in 2011, happens when:
options: Lava melts the foundations of buildings
Water-saturated loose ground momentarily behaves as a liquid, so intact buildings lean and settle
Rivers burst their banks during shaking
The sea floor is displaced vertically

questions.question: Chile's magnitude 8,8 earthquake in 2010 killed far fewer people than Haiti's magnitude 7,0 the same year mainly because:
options: Chile's earthquake was actually weaker
Haiti has more earthquakes each year
Chile's strictly enforced engineering codes kept collapse rare, while Haiti's unreinforced buildings failed — deaths follow vulnerability, not magnitude
Chile had no cities near the epicentre

questions.question: Since no scientist can put a date on the next earthquake, the working strategy is preparedness, which includes:
options: Evacuating all cities permanently
Waiting for an official prediction
Building only on soft sediment
Base isolation and braced buildings, zoning that keeps schools and hospitals off faults and soft ground, rehearsed drills, and networks giving seconds of warning

questions.question: In the branch picture, the long slow bend before the crack stands for:
options: Years of strain quietly loading the locked fault while nothing visible happens
The aftershocks
The surface waves
The tsunami crossing the ocean

questions.question: If the rock gave way five kilometres beneath the school hall, then:
options: The school hall is the focus
The point five kilometres down is the FOCUS and the school hall is the EPICENTRE
Both points are called the epicentre
The epicentre is five kilometres from the school

questions.question: The firecracker in the rain tank explains that:
options: Water causes most earthquakes
Deep and shallow earthquakes feel identical
A shallow focus is like the firecracker just under the lid — its energy arrives almost unspent, which is why shallow events flatten towns
Sound travels faster than shaking

subtopics.title: The Starter's Gun and Three Cell Towers

questions.question: The three 'runners' in arrival order are:
options: The P-wave squeeze, the S-wave whip, then the rolling surface wave
The surface wave, the P-wave, then the S-wave
The S-wave, the surface wave, then the P-wave
All three tie at the finish

questions.question: The starter's-gun comparison — smoke seen instantly, bang arriving later — teaches that:
options: Light and sound travel at the same speed
The gap between two signals that left together announces the distance to their source
Earthquakes can be heard before they are felt
Timekeepers cause the delay

questions.question: The cell-tower comparison shows that finding the epicentre requires:
options: One very sensitive station
A station exactly at the epicentre
Several distances at once — three stations, three circles, one crossing point
A phone signal from the fault

questions.question: The 'demolition crew' among the waves is:
options: The P-wave, because it arrives first
The S-wave, because it drowns in liquid
The foreshock
The surface wave — slowest, but it moves the ground furthest

subtopics.title: One Splash, Many Ripples — and Staying Alive

questions.question: In the dam picture, the single splash and the ripples reaching each shoreline stand for:
options: Richter magnitude — one number at the source — and Mercalli intensity, a different reading at every place
Mercalli at the source and Richter at the shore
The focus and the epicentre
Foreshocks and aftershocks

questions.question: Writing 'a bit stronger' about a magnitude 8 versus a magnitude 6 is wrong because two steps mean:
options: Twice the shaking
A hundred times the ground movement and about a thousand times the energy
Ten per cent more energy
Only the depth has changed

questions.question: The 'shallow muddy end of the dam' with its biggest waves corresponds to:
options: Bedrock towns that barely feel the shaking
The epicentre of every earthquake
Soft ground that amplifies shaking, giving odd patches of high Mercalli readings
The deepest part of the ocean

questions.question: The Chile-Haiti comparison from 2010 proves that:
options: Bigger earthquakes always kill more people
Small earthquakes are harmless
Death tolls are decided by luck
Deaths follow vulnerability: the far more powerful Chilean event killed a tiny fraction of Haiti's toll, because Chile builds, inspects and drills
